queries.name: Needle in a haystack
queries.why: The single most common on-call action: find one rare string across the whole window. Rewards an inverted index; punishes a full scan.

queries.name: Full-scan aggregation
queries.why: Count every record in the window grouped by level. No index helps; this is raw scan throughput over the whole corpus.

pulsetrace.unsupported: PulseTrace has no aggregation API for logs. The log surface exposes filters and a row limit, not GROUP BY — a user cannot ask this question at all. This is dimension D3 (query power) measured rather than asserted, and it is what phase P3 exists to fix.

queries.name: High-cardinality group-by
queries.why: Top customers by error volume across 50k distinct customer_id values. This is where a columnar store and an inverted index diverge most, and the dimension vendor benchmarks usually omit.

pulsetrace.unsupported: Same ceiling as the full-scan aggregation: no GROUP BY, so a 50k-cardinality ranking is not expressible against the log API.

queries.name: Trace by ID
queries.why: Point lookup of one trace. Pure index seek — should be fast on both, and a slow result here indicates a missing or unused index rather than a scan cost.

queries.name: Regex scan
queries.why: A regex over the message field. Defeats term indexes on both sides, so it measures the decompress-and-match path — the query class that most often surprises people on their bill.

queries.name: Time-narrowed service filter
queries.why: The default dashboard query: one service, one level, a short recent window. Both sides can express it, so it is the fairest head-to-head latency number in the suite and the one closest to real interactive use.
